title: Roll devbin out to the second fleet: eight more projects
objective: Install devbin into six more projects -- Multiplyer, Arca/arca_config, Arca/arca_cli, MicroGPTEx, Molt, Prolix -- one work package each, resolving each project's accumulated drift (elixir deps especially) as part of the process. Molt has a real dev launcher and gets the full ST0001 migration protocol; the other five are fresh installs. Two surveyed candidates are parked by hv's review of 2026-08-10: Pplr (to be redone as a Rust project) and Utilz (the beside-the-product shape needs more thought) -- WP-06 and WP-07 hold their rulings and survey facts.
context: ST0001 built the framework and rolled it onto the first fleet of four (plus devbin itself); this thread is the second fleet. These projects are older and quieter -- last substantive touches range from 2025-07 (Pplr) to 2026-08 (arca pair, Utilz) -- so the work per project is drift resolution plus install, not just install. The survey findings, the two path protocols, the elixir deps-drift protocol, and the per-project rulings live in `design.md`; the seeded acceptance contract is `acceptance.md`; the order and why is `tasks.md`. Planned under Fable 2026-08-10 for execution by a later session: the documents carry everything.

wps.title: CANCELLED -- Multiplyer: fresh install, and the deps-drift protocol proven
wps.body:
## CANCELLED by hv, 2026-08-10 -- Multiplyer is EOL

**Multiplyer is being retired, not migrated.** It moves to `_Archive`; the parts worth keeping are extracted from there into a new project, **Riffle**, built with Intent and devbin from the outset. Devbin is never installed into Multiplyer, so this WP has no work in it.

The decision came from hv's Fable review, after this WP's toolchain leg had already run. Multiplyer was written for a consumer project that died, and nothing has driven it since -- which is why its defects could sit undisturbed for a year.

Cancelled rather than deleted: the survey facts and the sequencing reasoning below are what a WP-06/WP-07-style park preserves, and Riffle inherits some of it.

## What ran anyway, and where it is recorded

The toolchain leg executed early, during WP-03, on hv's explicit instruction to fix the fleet toolchain. It is recorded in full at `WP/01/multiplyer-toolchain.md` beside this file, and landed as Multiplyer `c8a7a51b`. That work is now history in a repository about to be archived. **It is not to be revisited, reverted or built on.**

Its findings are not entirely wasted. Multiplyer's own **ST0042** (`Modernise Multiplyer: salvage, open-source, retire`) catalogues, with evidence, what is dead in there: the SIA pipeline yields no results at all, `.pred` file loading has never worked, `parameter_mappings` is a field no struct declares, and file logging had been silently dead since 2025-07-20. That is the salvage triage, written down before the decision to retire -- **read it in `_Archive` when picking pieces for Riffle rather than rediscovering it.**

## What this cancellation changes elsewhere

- **ST0002 is FIVE projects, not six**: MicroGPTEx (done), arca_config (done), arca_cli (in flight), Molt, Prolix.
- **WP-03's ordering note is now stale in its reasoning, not its conclusion.** It said "WP-01 Multiplyer branch-deps on THIS project too, so WP-01 waits on this one landing." Nothing downstream waits on arca_cli now. WP-03 proceeds unchanged; the argument for its position no longer applies.
- **The deps-drift protocol loses its hardest planned test.** It was proven at WP-04 on the gentlest possible ground and was to be stressed here -- 122 lib files on Ash, igniter, ecto and instructor, against the oldest pin in either fleet. No remaining WP replaces that. The protocol's strength therefore remains unproven, and design.md should not claim otherwise.
- **Riffle, when it exists, is a greenfield adoption** -- closer to WP-04 than to any `scripts/` migration. Whether it becomes a WP under this thread or its own steel thread is hv's call at the time.

## Acceptance

Declared `acceptance: exempt`. There is no work to accept.

The ACs this WP carried (AC-01.1 to AC-01.5) are retired in `acceptance.md` with the same ruling. **AC-01.4 was already recorded as unsatisfiable** -- seals are minted by `bin/devbin`, devbin was never installed at Multiplyer, and no pre-bump baseline was obtainable because the original dep set does not compile on OTP 29 at all. It is retired unmet, not retired satisfied.

## Dependencies

None. This WP does not run.

**Devbin is never installed into Molt.** hv's ruling on reading the inventory below: Molt is out of scope for this thread, not reshaped into a beside-the-product WP. Nothing further executes here.

Cancelled rather than deleted, on the WP-01 pattern: the inventory, the eleven dispositions and the collision probe are the record, and the probe in particular is the thing WP-06 was parked wanting.

**The frontmatter still says `status: WIP`, and that is not a mistake to correct in passing.** There is no `intent wp cancel`, so the status field belongs to the CLI and only `start` and `done` can write it. `Done` would claim work that never happened; the title prefix carries the ruling instead, as at WP-01. **A reader of `intent wp list ST0002` will see WP-05 as WIP -- it is not. Read the title.**

**What this cancellation changes elsewhere**:

- **ST0002 is FOUR projects, not five**: MicroGPTEx (done), arca_config (done), arca_cli (done), Prolix. **WP-08 Prolix is the only work left in this thread.**
- **The thread never proves the shell shape.** Molt was to be the one shell migration; every remaining project is elixir. `shell` and `swift` gate scope now reach WP-08 unexercised, which is a fact about WP-08's risk, not a reason to reopen anything.
- **WP-06's dependency line is void.** It reads "WP-05 (shell shape proven)"; there is no WP-05 to prove it. What WP-06 actually gains is the collision probe below, already run and passed.

## The finding that stopped it, 2026-08-10 -- the brief would have deleted the product

**`bin/molt` is Molt's product CLI, not a dev launcher.** It is symlinked into `~/bin` on every machine the user owns; its commands are `resleeve`, `upgrade`, `maintain`, `new-user`. `bin/bootstrap.sh` is the **public installer**, documented as a `curl` one-liner against a raw GitHub URL, so its path is an external contract.

The objective and deliverables below were written from the 2026-08-10 survey, which classified `bin/` by line count without opening the files. Followed literally -- "old launcher deleted last" -- they destroy the tool this project ships. **Nothing has been installed into Molt.**

**Molt is a beside-the-product project, which is the shape hv PARKED at WP-06** ("the beside-the-product shape needs more thought before devbin enters Utilz"). WP-06's dependency line reads "WP-05 (shell shape proven)" -- the sequencing assumed a straightforward shell migration here would de-risk the hard case there. There is no straightforward shell migration in this thread; Molt and Utilz are the same problem.

Full evidence, all eleven command dispositions, and the collision probe: `molt-inventory.md` beside this file.

~~**Three things need hv's ruling before this WP moves**: whether it runs as a beside-the-product install or parks alongside WP-06; what the devbin entry is called, given `bin/molt` is taken and stays taken; and whether `molt test` -- the one genuine dev/product overlap -- stays in the product or moves.~~ **Answered by cancellation: none of them arise. Molt keeps `bin/molt`, keeps `bin/bootstrap.sh`, and keeps `molt test` as the way it tests itself.**

The one change this WP left in Molt is unrelated to devbin and stands: `46231e7` removes a stale `elixir` language declaration for a project with no Elixir in it. It was a real defect found on the way past, not a migration step.

## Deliverables

- ~~Inventory of both scripts with a disposition per command and every authored ruling extracted before any prose moves~~ **DONE**: `molt-inventory.md`. This is what stopped the WP.
- ~~Fence, install alongside, both launchers coexisting until the switch~~ -> install alongside stands; **there is no switch**
- ~~Equivalence pack: every old command run both ways and compared~~ -> **no equivalence to prove**; nothing is being replaced. The bats suite must be green through devbin.

- ~~`bootstrap.sh` gets its own disposition~~ **DONE**: keep beside, untouched, out of scope. It is a published install path.
- Entry naming ruled by hv, as WP-06 (`bin/molt` is taken; probe used `mt`; `bin/devbin` alone is viable)

Acceptance Criteria for this work package live in the steel thread's `acceptance.md`, under the `WP-05` heading (single source of truth). Do not restate ACs here.

wps.body:
## RECLASSIFIED before start, 2026-08-10: this is a migration, and one entry is on hold

**Prolix has no `bin/` at all and a twelve-entry, 235-line `scripts/` fleet. This is a `scripts/` migration, not a fresh install.** The brief below was written from a survey that read `bin/` and counted lines; it is the third in this thread to be wrong that way, and the first corrected BEFORE the WP started rather than at its close. AC-08.5 to AC-08.8 are added for the migration half. Inventory: `prolix-inventory.md` beside this file.

**A live production credential is committed to this repository, and it gates one entry.** `scripts/flysql:15` holds a plaintext password for the `geodica-db` cluster, reaching `conflab_prod`, `laksa_prod` and `prolix_prod` -- three production databases across three projects. It is in git history (`f21484b`, `5f78f3b`), so deleting the file removes nothing; only rotation does, and that is hv's. **`flysql` is ON HOLD: not ported, not moved, not rewritten, not deleted.** The reason it is called out at WP level rather than left in the inventory is that a migration's default behaviour -- transcribe the script into a handler -- would copy the credential into a new file and put a fresh timestamp on it.

**Two premises in the brief below are void.** Its `Dependencies` names WP-01 as "the elixir protocol"; WP-01 is cancelled, and the protocol was proven at WP-02/03/04. And it is no longer "last ... on top of a by-then boring elixir path": it is the ONLY WP left in the thread, and Molt's cancellation means `shell` and `swift` gate scope both reach it unexercised, on the project that also carries the first live deploy-image arm.

## As built, 2026-08-10 -- CLOSED 8/8

Ten commits at Prolix: fence `312c3d3`, deps `2abecde`, Oban `5408034`, install `e5c7d4f`, config `81de3fa`, lockfile tidy `f6826e5`, warnings count `9fd6d5b`, re-vendor `8f8b229`, port `9dd4940`, toolchain `e4bc604`, deletion `201b69b`. Record: `prolix-inventory.md` for the dispositions, `equivalence.md` for the twelve proven rows.

**The last WP of the thread found two defects in the base, and both were the same shape underneath: a code path nothing had ever executed.**

- **Issue 0010** -- `check format`'s swift arm ran `swift-format --lint`, an option the tool has never had; it dispatches on a subcommand. The arm had never run anywhere, because devbin's own repository has no `.swift` files and the determinate-zero path returns green before reaching the command line. Correcting the subcommand then walked into the second half: `swift-format lint` exits 0 WITH findings, so the fixed arm examined 78 files, printed 633 findings, and sealed GREEN. **Fixing a hard error had produced a gate incapable of failing** -- caught only by reading the empty `.errors` file against a terminal full of findings.
- **Issue 0011** -- a config `run:` on a catalogue OPTION silently unsealed it. `test swift` ran, xcodebuild printed `** TEST FAILED **`, and no verdict file was written at all. The exit code was correct throughout, which is what hid it. And every project in the first fleet had been working around this by hand, restating `log:` in its config with a comment explaining that it must -- so the first person to trust the Highlander rule and NOT duplicate got an unsealed gate.

Both were red-checked with tests before being fixed; devbin's suite went 523 -> 526.

**What the migration repaired rather than preserved.** `scripts/cli`'s `REPL_MODE=true` prefix was redundant AND actively harmful: it won over the caller's environment, so `REPL_MODE=false` -- this project's own documented "show me the logs" override, named as a feature in its own completed ST0011 -- could not be reached through the script at all. Measured at 84 bytes either way with the prefix, 971 without it through the builtin. Dropping it restored a feature that had never worked.

**What was found on the way past and handed to hv, not actioned**: three committed credentials in three shapes (hv's 2026-08-10 ruling covered one of them), a CI credo step running zero checks over 267 files, the deploy image trailing the pins, and 632 swift formatting findings. All in `equivalence.md` and mirrored into Prolix ST0028.

**What this WP found and handed off**: Prolix's lockfile had not moved since 2026-02-21, carrying 22 vulnerable packages and 66 advisories (2 CRITICAL), and would not compile on Elixir 1.20.3 at all. That is now ZERO advisories, a booting suite at 746 passed, and `mix.exs` two unused dependencies lighter. The remaining dependency work -- nine constraint-blocked majors, 11 compile warnings, the toolchain pin -- is **Prolix ST0028**, raised on hv's ruling so it is sized as its own thread rather than smuggled into a devbin migration.

**Still to do here**: the swift arms (AC-08.3), the toolchain arm (AC-08.4, blocked behind ST0028's pin decision), equivalence for all twelve `scripts/` entries with the `REPL_MODE` probe and the `--trace` delta (AC-08.5 to 08.7), and the `scripts/` deletion last on hv's go.

## Deliverables

- Fence, one install commit, doctor green, `help --why` accounted
- Baseline -> `mix deps.update --all` -> green per protocol (elixir path)
- Swift arms exercised against `native/ios` via config overrides; every builtin-row shortfall filed as a base finding, never patched locally
- `check toolchain` green including the image arm against the real Dockerfile; the `.tool-versions` question surfaced to hv (add per fleet norm, or record absence)
- Deploy proof deferred to the owner's next `fly deploy`, per the ST0001 pattern

## Dependencies

- ~~The elixir protocol (WP-01) and, softly, everything before it -- last by design~~ **WP-01 is CANCELLED.** The elixir protocol was proven at WP-02, WP-03 and WP-04, all Done, so this dependency is satisfied by different work than it names.
- **hv's ruling on the `flysql` credential** before that one entry moves. Nothing else in the WP waits on it.

# WP-01 note -- Multiplyer's toolchain leg landed before the WP opened

Multiplyer commit `c8a7a51b`, made during WP-03, not WP-01. This note exists so the WP does not later read its own ACs as satisfied by work that did not follow the protocol.

## Why it happened here

hv's instruction on 2026-08-10 was to fix the fleet toolchain "properly ... on the latest versions of everything we can be", and Multiplyer was named as the dangerous outstanding case: its `.tool-versions` said `elixir 1.18.0` / `erlang 27.0` while every local run used 1.20.3 / OTP 29, and that file is CI's only source. Fixing the pin is what dragged the rest in, because Multiplyer did not compile clean on the compiler it was already being developed on.

That was not a decision to start WP-01. It was the toolchain leg of WP-01 arriving early, on hv's explicit go, in a project where devbin is not installed yet.

## The protocol deviation, stated plainly

**AC-01.4 asks for baseline seals BEFORE `mix deps.update --all` and green seals after. There are no seals, and there cannot be.** Seals are minted by `bin/devbin`, and devbin is not installed at Multiplyer -- that is WP-01's own first deliverable. The dependency resolution ran under bare `mix`.

Worse, and recorded rather than glossed: **the first full-suite run was taken AFTER the dep bumps, not before.** No pre-bump baseline is obtainable on this machine either, because the original dep set does not compile on OTP 29 at all -- `meck` 0.9.x fails hard there (`catch ...` is a syntax error on OTP 29), which is why it is overridden past `mock`'s `~> 0.9.2` constraint. So the "before" side of the comparison never existed.

What stands in its place is weaker and should be read as weaker: five consecutive green full-suite runs after the fact, with zero warnings, plus `compile --warnings-as-errors`, `format`, `credo` and `intent critic` all clean. That proves the end state. It does not prove the change was inert, and nothing here claims it was.

## What this means for WP-01 when it opens

- **AC-01.3 is satisfied**, and by its first branch: the pins are bumped on record. It is NOT in its own commit -- it rides `c8a7a51b` with the whole migration -- which is a lesser deviation worth knowing about when reading the history.
- **AC-01.4 cannot be satisfied as written.** The WP must either restate it for a project whose deps were already resolved before devbin arrived, or record it as knowingly unmet. It must not be ticked on the strength of the green runs above; that is exactly the false green this thread keeps catching.
- **The remaining WP-01 ACs are untouched.** No `.prettierignore` fence, no install, no `doctor`, no `help --why`. AC-01.1, AC-01.2 and AC-01.5 are all still open, and WP-01 is still a fresh install in every respect that matters.

## What the leg turned up

Multiplyer went from 24 compiler warnings to 0, and most were real defects rather than noise. Two gates were found passing while examining nothing: `mix credo --only error` ran zero checks (credo has no `error` category), and file logging had been silently dead since 2025-07-20 because `config :logger, backends:` stopped being read. An async filesystem race in the test suite was failing roughly one run in three or four.

Full detail, with evidence, is in Multiplyer's own **ST0042** (`Modernise Multiplyer: salvage, open-source, retire`), raised on hv's instruction. The salvage question -- Multiplyer's consumer project died, and what survives should be open-sourced rather than maintained whole -- is that thread's, not this one's.

**The finding that matters to ST0002**: five SIA pipeline tests were strengthened and failed 5 of 5. The pipeline produces no results, and `if not Enum.empty?(results) do ... end` with the comment "be flexible" had hidden it. They are now characterisation tests that go red when the pipeline works. A WP that installs devbin at Multiplyer and runs `test mix` will see green over a suite that contains five deliberately-pinned defects; that is by design, and this note is where it is written down.

# WP-02 inventory -- `scripts/` at arca_config

The thread's first migration off hv's OLDER launcher convention (`scripts/`, pre-devbin), as distinct from ST0001's `bin/<prj>` convention. Three tracked files, sixteen lines. A disposition for every one, and the disposition is only partly a port: most of what these scripts do is already done, correctly, somewhere else.

## The three commands

| Script          | What it runs                                                                | Disposition                                          |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `scripts/cli`   | loads `config/.env` if present, then `exec mix arca.config "$@"`            | `commands.cli.run: mix arca.config`                  |
| `scripts/iex`   | `.env`, `ARCA_CONFIG_PATH=.arca`, `iex -S mix Arca.Config $*`               | `bin/ac iex` -- the builtin (CORRECTED, see below)   |
| `scripts/test`  | `.env`, `ARCA_CONFIG_PATH=.arca`, `mix test --trace $*`                     | `commands.test.options.mix.run` at CI's strictness   |

`scripts/gh` is an EMPTY directory. Git does not track empty directories, so it has never been in the repository; it goes with the rest.

## Three things the port deliberately does NOT carry

**1. The `.env` loading, in all three.** `config/dotenv.exs` is imported by `config.exs` and loads `config/.env` during mix configuration evaluation, on every dev and test invocation. Its header records that it was fixed to be defaults-not-overrides ("a variable you exported before running `mix test` was silently replaced"), and it tolerates a missing file. So mix has been doing this correctly all along, and the shell preamble in all three scripts is redundant -- `scripts/cli` doing it carefully, `scripts/iex` and `scripts/test` doing it with the fragile `export $(cat ./config/.env | grep -v "^#" | xargs)` form that fails outright on a fresh clone.

That fragile form is itself a Highlander breach the project half-fixed: `scripts/cli` carries a comment saying it "used to fail outright in that case because `cat` on a missing file aborted the command". The fix landed in one of three copies. The port does not carry any of them.

**2. `ARCA_CONFIG_PATH=.arca`, in `iex` and `test`.** It is DEAD and it is a TRAP, and both halves come from the same precedence table (`lib/config/cfg.ex:36-37`):

    tier 1 (highest)  <DOMAIN>_CONFIG_PATH   -- here ARCA_CONFIG_CONFIG_PATH
    tier 2            ARCA_CONFIG_PATH       -- the generic fallback

`config/.env` sets the tier-1 variable to `.arca_config`. The scripts set the tier-2 one to `.arca`. Tier 1 wins, so the scripts' value never takes effect -- **unless `config/.env` goes missing**, which is precisely the fresh-clone case, and then the suite writes `.arca/` into the working tree. `.gitignore` ignores `/.arca_config/` and NOT `/.arca/`, so it would land as untracked repository dirt.

The project has already ruled against this, in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: *"ARCA_CONFIG_CONFIG_PATH used to be set here to `.arca_config`, inside the checkout, which is how test writes ended up in the repository."* The fix landed in CI and never in `scripts/test`. It is also redundant twice over -- `test/test_helper.exs:17` points the suite at `System.tmp_dir!()/arca_config_suite_<unique>` itself and fails the run on drift.

**3. `mix test --trace`.** `--trace` is output verbosity, not gate strictness, and it is a per-invocation preference: devbin passes trailing argv through, so `bin/ac test mix --trace` still works. What the row runs instead is CI's line, `mix test --warnings-as-errors`, because the catalogue's plain `mix test` would make devbin's gate check LESS than the gate beside it -- CI's comment is explicit that plain `mix compile` misses test-file warnings, which is why it added the flag.

## Equivalence

| Old                      | New                                | Same?                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `scripts/cli <args>`     | `bin/ac cli <args>`                | same task, same argv; `.env` via dotenv.exs instead of shell |
| `scripts/iex`            | `bin/ac iex`                       | same running system; loses a startup banner and `$*`         |
|                          |                                    | pass-through -- see the correction below                     |
| `scripts/test <args>`    | `bin/ac test mix <args>`           | STRICTER on purpose: gains `--warnings-as-errors`, loses a   |
|                          |                                    | default `--trace` (still available as an argument) and loses |
|                          |                                    | a dead env var that only ever fired on a broken checkout     |

Two of the three are behaviour-preserving. `test` is deliberately not: it gets stricter, and it stops carrying a hazard. Both differences are recorded here rather than smoothed over, per hv's fleet norm on surfacing project dirt.

## The `iex` row was wrong, and how

This row first read `bin/ac cli --iex`, justified as "the framework's own `--iex` option (D20)", and the equivalence cell proved that `mix Arca.Config` and `mix arca.config` resolve to the same module. That is true, and it was the wrong half to check. **The claim at risk was that `--iex` makes `cli` run under IEx, and nobody ran it.** It does not: `DEVBIN_OPT_IEX` is read by exactly one thing in devbin, the builtin `server` handler, which is `enabled: false` here -- and for a declared `run:` nothing reads it at all. `bin/ac cli --iex` is parsed, exported and ignored.

Caught while authoring the `cli` help topic -- the last deliverable of the WP -- by writing the flag down and then testing it with a poisoned `iex` first on PATH: it never fired for `cli --iex`, and fired immediately for `bin/ac iex`. `scripts/iex` had already been deleted in `2522cfb` on the strength of the wrong disposition.

**Nothing was lost.** The builtin `iex` command (`iex -S mix`) is offered and live here and is what actually replaces the script. The delta, now recorded rather than assumed: `scripts/iex` ran `iex -S mix Arca.Config`, which is the builtin plus running the CLI task at startup, so it printed a usage banner before the prompt and could pass `$*` through to that invocation. The app starts either way, so the running system is identical; from inside the session `Arca.Config.CLI.main(["list"])` covers the argument case better than the shell form did.

The base defect this rested on is filed as **Devbin issue 0009** -- `--iex` is offered on the language axis but read by one built-in -- which is issue 0001's own deferred question, now answered by evidence. arca_config's config.yaml comment (`14ce8ef`) and its authored `help/iex.md` (`f5e170a`) both carry the corrected fact.

The general lesson, and it is the sharper form of a watch-out already on the board: **an equivalence table proves the half you thought to check.** This one had a cell with a true statement in it, which is what made it look done -- the untested claim was not in the table at all.

## The seals

    baseline  check  20260810-1040.{COMPILE,FORMAT,CRITIC} 0 bytes
                     20260810-1040.DEPS       262 bytes  -- ten unused lockfile entries
                     20260810-1040.TOOLCHAIN  156 bytes  -- no .tool-versions

    after     check  20260810-1201.* all 0 bytes

`mix deps.update --all` moved NOTHING -- the lockfile came back byte-identical, `optimus` unchanged at `4abb595f`. Recorded as a proven no-op rather than skipped: the step was initially missed on this WP and caught by reading the ACs against what had been done, which is what the ACs are for.

`optimus` is a GitHub branch dep on `matthewsinclair/arca-optimus`, out of this thread's scope. It will move under this project whenever that repo moves; recorded, not chased. Same class as Multiplyer's `arca_dbutils`.

## What the migration turned out to be: mostly deletion

Three scripts, sixteen lines, and the port is one config line plus a builtin that was already offered.

- **The `.env` preamble in all three was redundant.** `config/dotenv.exs` already loads `config/.env` during mix config evaluation, defaults-not-overrides, tolerant of a missing file. The scripts were doing by hand what the framework does properly.
- **`scripts/iex` did not become a command; it became the builtin `iex`.** It ran `iex -S mix Arca.Config`, which is `iex -S mix` plus running the CLI task at startup. Recorded FIRST as `bin/ac cli --iex` and that was wrong -- see below.
- **`ARCA_CONFIG_PATH=.arca` was dead AND a trap.** `cfg.ex:36-37` puts `<DOMAIN>_CONFIG_PATH` above the generic one, and `config/.env` sets the domain variable, so the scripts' value never fired -- until `config/.env` is missing, which is the fresh-clone case, and then the suite writes `.arca/` into the checkout (`.gitignore` covers `/.arca_config/`, not `/.arca/`). The project had ALREADY ruled against this, in `ci.yml`: *"which is how test writes ended up in the repository."* The fix landed in CI and never in `scripts/test`. Not carried.

One deliberate non-equivalence: `test mix` runs CI's `mix test --warnings-as-errors` rather than the catalogue's bare `mix test`, because a gate that checks LESS than the gate beside it passes every comparison you would think to make. `--trace`, which the old script hard-coded, is output verbosity and remains available as a pass-through argument.

Equivalence proven through the new entry point: `cli --help` and `cli --version` byte-identical to `scripts/cli`'s, and the suite green and unchanged either side (baseline seal `20260810-1040.MIX`, after `20260810-1201.MIX`, both `.errors` 0 bytes).

## The one row that was not proven, and what it cost

**`scripts/iex`'s disposition was wrong, it was recorded as proven, and it was caught by the WP's last deliverable.**

The inventory's equivalence row read `scripts/iex` -> `bin/ac cli --iex`, justified as devbin's framework-owned `--iex` (D20), with the cell asserting that `mix Arca.Config` and `mix arca.config` resolve to the same module. That is true. **It is also not the claim that could fail.** The claim that could fail was "`--iex` makes `cli` run under IEx", and it was never tested -- the row proved a true irrelevance beside an untested assertion, which is exactly what made it read as done.

`DEVBIN_OPT_IEX` is read by one thing in the whole framework, the builtin `server` handler (`grep -rln DEVBIN_OPT_IEX lib/cmd/` returns it alone). `server` is `enabled: false` here, and a declared `run:` reads nothing. So `bin/ac cli --iex` is parsed, exported and ignored. `scripts/iex` had been deleted in `2522cfb` two commits earlier.

Found while authoring `help/cli.md` -- writing down what the flag does forced the question, and the poisoned-binary probe answered it: a fake `iex` first on PATH never fired for `bin/ac cli --iex` (output byte-identical to the plain run), and fired immediately for `bin/ac iex`.

**Nothing was lost.** The builtin `iex` command is offered and live here, and it is the real replacement. The delta is now recorded rather than assumed: the old script printed a CLI usage banner before the prompt and could pass `$*` to that startup invocation; the app starts either way, so the running system is identical, and `Arca.Config.CLI.main(["list"])` from the prompt covers the argument case better.

Corrected in three places, because a wrong reason recorded once gets read many times: arca_config's config.yaml (`14ce8ef`), its authored `help/iex.md` (`f5e170a`), and the inventory beside this file. The base defect is **Devbin issue 0009**, which turns out to be issue 0001's own deferred question -- "is the right key the language, or the consuming command?" -- answered by evidence a day after 0001 chose the language for want of any.

## The toolchain answer was reversed the same day

**hv, 2026-08-10, during WP-03: `check toolchain` is LIVE here, and there is no per-project judgement to make.** Commit `f3d91c8` adds `.tool-versions` at the fleet's pins, guards the CI cell that claims to track them, and removes the `enabled: false`. Gates green with the arm armed -- eight seals at `20260810-1413`, all 0 bytes.

This WP had disabled the arm, reasoning that CI's matrix was already the home for the fact and a pin file would be a second one. Wrong twice:

- **On the facts.** The matrix's top cell said `1.20.2` while every local run used `1.20.3`, and the comment above it claimed the cell tracked the toolchain the library is developed on. The fact that supposedly had a home had already drifted, unwatched -- which is an argument FOR the gate, not against it. Reading the comment and not the value is what made the disable look reasoned.
- **On the policy.** hv's rule has been in Baize's own `.tool-versions` header since 2026-07-28: *"run the latest, and keep this file matching what you actually run."* It is fleet-wide. The "three shapes" rule in design.md was derived here from one project's CI layout, when the corpus already carried the answer.

A CI matrix is not a competing home. The pin file is the version the library is DEVELOPED on; the matrix's lower cells are the versions it still SUPPORTS, which is worth keeping for a published library. Two facts, one home each -- and only the cell that claims to track local is a copy, so only that cell is guarded.

## The credo driveby, and what it cost

hv asked for credo "if it's easy as a driveby". Adding the dep was easy; making the gate green was not, and the shape is worth recording for the next four projects:

- First `--strict` run: **139 findings**. 129 of them were ONE check, `Credo.Check.Design.AliasUsage`, and 116 of those were in test files.
- Ruled out project-wide in `.credo.exs` -- in credo's config file, not devbin's, so the devbin row stays at the fleet's `--strict` default with no config entry. A laxer command line in the launcher would put a project style ruling in the wrong file.
- The remaining **ten were real**. Nine fixed: alias ordering twice, parens on a no-arg def, explicit `try` -> implicit, a private `is_prefix?` -> `prefix?`, a redundant last `with` clause, an inverted negated if-else, `10000` -> `10_000`, and `flatten_and_cache` un-nested from depth three into a guard clause plus a per-entry function.
- **The tenth was credo being wrong, and the code already said so.** `callback_test` uses `apply/3` deliberately, to keep a wrong arity away from the compiler's static check while exercising the runtime `FunctionClauseError`; its comment explains this. It got an inline disable naming the check, not a rewrite.

**The project caught a mistake of mine.** `deps_audit_test` asserts every dependency in `mix.exs` carries a written reason, and it failed the instant credo appeared without one -- turning a driveby into a documented decision at the moment of the change. It is a good test and worth copying.

# WP-03 record -- arca_cli, and the base feature it forced

## Reclassified, like WP-02 before it

The WP is titled "fresh install". It is a **migration**: `scripts/` carries 220 lines across 9 entries. Design.md already counted arca_cli among the four `scripts/` projects; the WP title and its ACs were written from the survey and never caught up. Same reclassification as WP-02, same cause -- a survey row that recorded a conclusion the design later corrected.

## The launcher name

`bin/arca_cli`, alias **`bin/acli`** (hv, 2026-08-10). The alias convention across the Arca pair is `acli` / `acfg`; arca_config currently ships `ac` and is to be renamed to `acfg` as a follow-up on a closed WP.

## Commits

| # | Commit    | What                                                              |
| - | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | `4f2d047` | the `.prettierignore` fence, ahead of the install                 |
| 2 | `f12a63f` | `.tool-versions` at the fleet's pins, CI greps anchored           |
| 3 | `21f0ce2` | the single install commit; doctor 9 checks / 0 failed             |
| 4 | `d62dcf0` | config from the inventory, and the completions file it needs      |

## The base feature this WP forced: `project.cli_task`

**`mix arca.cli`, not `mix arca_cli.cli`.** devbin derives the CLI task from the project name; the real task is `Mix.Tasks.Arca.Cli` because the module namespace is `Arca` and the directory is `arca_cli`. The two do not have to agree, and here they do not.

Fixed in the base rather than worked around locally, because `repl` cannot take a `run:` override without losing rlwrap -- the very thing that makes shipping a `repl` builtin worthwhile. One config line now feeds both `cli` and `repl`.

## Devbin issue 0009, proven in the field

`commands.server.enabled: false` -- a library and a CLI framework has nothing to serve. Under the 0009 fix that **also withdraws `--iex`**, and it does: `help --why` lists `server` under "not offered here" with its reason, and no `Shared options` block appears at all. Before 0009 the flag was offered wherever `elixir` was declared and silently ignored everywhere nothing read it.

`bin/acli cli --iex` now exits 1 with arca_cli's own `error: --iex: unknown command`. That is devbin's designed pass-through, not a defect: `lib/resolve` states it -- *"An undeclared `--flag` is NOT an error -- it passes through to the handler, which is what lets `devbin test mix --trace` reach mix."* The refusal message is for the other case, where the option IS live but the command cannot read it.

## Equivalence -- every claim that could fail, tested

**The WP-02 lesson applied: name the claim that could FAIL and test THAT.** A true statement beside an untested one is what makes a row look done.

| old                  | new                | claim tested                          | result                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scripts/cli`        | `bin/acli cli`     | same output                           | `--help`, `--version`, `about` all **byte-identical**                      |
| `scripts/cli`        | `bin/acli cli`     | argv survives quoting                 | `$*` -> 3 args, `"$@"` -> 1; same rendered message. Improvement, no delta  |
| `scripts/test`       | `bin/acli test mix`| dropping `REPL_MODE` changes nothing  | **785 passed both ways**; seal `20260810-1642.MIX.errors` 0 bytes          |
| `scripts/iex`        | `bin/acli iex`     | what actually gets invoked            | poisoned `iex`: old `-S mix Arca.Cli`, new `-S mix`. **Real delta, below** |
| `scripts/repl`       | `bin/acli repl`    | which task, and is rlwrap wired       | poisoned `mix` + `rlwrap`; equivalent or better, below                     |

### The `iex` delta, measured rather than assumed

Old ran `iex -S mix Arca.Cli` -- the CLI task at startup, printing its usage banner, then an IEx prompt. New runs `iex -S mix`. The app is loaded identically either way; what is lost is the startup banner and `$*` pass-through to that invocation. `Arca.Cli.main(["about"])` from the prompt covers the argument case better than the old script did.

This is the row WP-02 got wrong. It is measured here before being written down.

### The `repl` delta

    old  rlwrap -f ./scripts/completions/completions.txt --complete-filenames \
           /bin/zsh -c "REPL_MODE=true mix Arca.Cli repl "
    new  rlwrap -f <abs>/bin/completions/repl.txt -r -c \
           -H ~/.arca_cli_repl_history -s 2000 mix arca.cli repl

Equivalent or better on every axis: completions wired both ways (absolute path now), and the new form adds persistent history (`-H`, `-s 2000`) and word memory (`-r`) that the old had no equivalent for. It also drops the wrapper shell, which existed only to carry `REPL_MODE=true`.

**A measurement artefact caught mid-probe, and worth recording.** The first old-side reading showed NO `-f` flag -- because this WP had already moved `scripts/completions/completions.txt`, so the old script's own lookup failed. That reading would have produced a false finding ("the old repl had no completions"). The file was restored temporarily to take a fair before-reading, then removed again. **A before/after comparison run after you have changed the "before" is not a comparison.**

## `REPL_MODE` is dead, and the project says so itself

All three of `scripts/{cli,iex,test}` and the `repl` wrapper exported `REPL_MODE=true`. It is not carried, and this is not a judgement call: `test/arca_cli/dead_code_gate_test.exs:43` asserts `sites("REPL_MODE") == []`, so the project has already ruled it out and gates it. The scripts were stale against their own project's invariant.

## Dispositions -- all nine entries

| entry                 | disposition                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cli`                 | `bin/acli cli` via `project.cli_task`                                          |
| `iex`                 | builtin `bin/acli iex`, delta recorded above                                   |

## Baseline seals

    check  20260810-1645.{COMPILE,FORMAT,DEPS,TOOLCHAIN,CRITIC}  all 0 bytes
    test   20260810-1646.MIX     0 bytes
           20260810-1646.CREDO   29366 bytes  -- RED, and a real finding

**The credo arm is red at baseline: 156 findings under devbin's `--strict` fleet default.** By check: 50 `AliasUsage`, 26 explicit `try`, 15 parens on no-arg defs, 13 `Enum.map_join`, 7 predicate naming, 7 nesting depth, 5 `length/1`, 5 negated if-else, 4 `apply/2,3`, plus a tail.

hv's ruling (2026-08-10): **record it red and size the remediation separately.** A red baseline arm is what AC-03.3 asks to be recorded, and absorbing a ~150-fix job into an install WP is the driveby-ceiling mistake. arca_config's precedent -- rule the dominant check out in `.credo.exs`, fix the real remainder -- turned on that remainder being ten. Here it is roughly a hundred.

There is no `.credo.exs` in this project yet.

## The deps leg -- unblocked, run, and what it did and did not prove

hv published the ten WP-02 commits and ran `mix deps.update --all` on 2026-08-10. Landed as `69510ca`.

Checked and cleared while the block was live: `arca-config` (hyphen) and `arca_config` (underscore) are the SAME GitHub repo -- `git ls-remote` returns one ref for both. Not a second repo, just a redirect.

**The baseline is provably a before-reading, not a reconstructed one.** The seals are stamped 16:45/16:46; the last commit (`d62dcf0`) is 16:41 and the lock's mtime after hv's update is 17:15, with a one-line diff against `HEAD` in between. So the baseline was taken on the pre-update lock, and nothing touched it in the gap. This matters because the repl probe on this same WP had already produced one artefact of exactly the opposite kind.

| leg      | baseline (pre-update) | post-update `20260810-1719` |
| -------- | --------------------- | --------------------------- |
| COMPILE  | 0 bytes               | 0 bytes                     |
| FORMAT   | 0 bytes               | 0 bytes                     |
| DEPS     | 0 bytes               | 0 bytes                     |
| TOOLCHAIN| 0 bytes               | 0 bytes                     |
| CRITIC   | 0 bytes -- **vacuous**| 0 bytes -- **vacuous**      |
| MIX      | 0 bytes               | 0 bytes                     |
| CREDO    | 29366 bytes RED       | 29366 bytes RED, byte-identical |

The credo seals `diff` clean: the same 156 findings, not one more. The mix leg reports the same 785 passed on both sides.

**Two things this leg did NOT prove, said plainly so the green is not read for more than it bought:**

- **The drift was one dep wide.** `mix deps.update --all` moved exactly one line of the lock -- arca_config `53805b77` -> `f3d91c84`. Every other dep was already at its resolvable best. This is a narrow test, closer to WP-04's gentle ground than to the stress the cancelled WP-01 was to have supplied.
- **`check critic` examined ZERO files, on both sides.** It scans the staging area, and the tree was clean, so it printed `nothing staged -- the critic will examine NO files` and sealed green. **That 0-byte seal is not evidence of anything and is not counted as such here.**

  Checked before raising it as a devbin defect, and it is not one: `lib/cmd/check:24-25` already rules on exactly this case -- *"With no arguments it defaults to --staged, and SAYS SO when nothing is staged. Silently examining zero files would pass for the same reason."* The warning lands in the sealed `.out`, so a seal-reader can see the arm was hollow without having watched the run. The design is sound; what is wrong is only a reader who takes `all check options passed` as coverage. That reader was me for about a minute, which is why it is written down here. Same lesson as issue 0003, from the other direction: there, a green gate hid a gap; here, a green gate declares its own gap and still needs reading.

**The published-API question was answered by reading, not by trusting the diffstat.** The upstream delta touches six `lib/` files, which is enough to require the read: alias reordering in `arca_config.ex` and `init_helper.ex`; a moduledoc line in `cli.ex` (`scripts/cli` -> `bin/ac cli`); `def notify_callbacks(), do:` losing its definition-site parens; `cache.ex` moving a `try/rescue` to a function-level `rescue` and renaming a `defp is_prefix?` to `prefix?`; `file_watcher.ex` collapsing a two-clause `with` and inverting an `if !`; `server.ex` moving the private `flatten_and_cache` onto guard clauses. Every one is internal. Names, arities, specs and return shapes are unchanged, so no consumer of `Arca.Config` resolves anything different and no hv ack was owed under the AC-02.3 rule.

## The deletion

hv's go given 2026-08-10. Seven scripts deleted in `b470476`, last of the five commits, and in ONE commit with their caller so a rollback is a single revert rather than a tree that half-believes in a directory.

**The caller survey was re-run, not reused.** The WP-start survey was a day old and the tree had moved since -- `bin/completions/` had been added, and that directory exists precisely because of a script being retired. Re-running it found the same single live caller, which is the reassuring outcome, but the point is that it was checked rather than assumed. Two matches in the same grep are unrelated directories that a careless search-and-delete would have caught: `.claude/scripts/` (Intent's session hooks) and `test/fixtures/scripts/` (a heredoc fixture). The four references under `intent/st/COMPLETED/` are deliberately left -- they record what was true when they were written, and rewriting them would falsify history.

**5.3.3 was rewritten, not search-replaced, because the mapping is not one-to-one.** `update_completions` has no successor at all: it inferred completions by grepping a REPL session for word-shaped tokens, and the data now lives in `bin/completions/repl.txt` as data. The rewrite also states the two things a newcomer cannot infer from a command list -- that verdicts are files under `tmp/` with an empty `.errors` as the green, and that `help --why` explains what is NOT offered.

Gates after: 785 passed, five check seals empty, credo seal byte-identical at 29366. The credo red being unchanged is the correct result, not a suspicious one: credo reads `lib/` and never read `scripts/`.

**One expectation that was wrong, and worth the correction.** Staging the deletion should have made `check critic` non-vacuous for the first time in this WP. It did not: staged *deletions* have no file to read, so it examined zero files again and said so per language. The `nothing staged` warning was suppressed, because something WAS staged. Right outcome by a narrower path than assumed -- the warning is about an empty index, not about an empty examination.

# WP-04 record -- MicroGPTEx, the fresh-install path proven

The first WP of the second fleet, and the first proof of the deps-drift protocol. Six commits in `~/Devel/prj/MicroGPTEx`, in this order, each its own fact.

| # | Commit    | What                                                                    |
| - | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | `b7cefc3` | the `.prettierignore` fence, proven here before it was relied on        |
| 2 | `54fca66` | `.tool-versions` -- erlang 29.0.5, elixir 1.20.3-otp-29 (hv's call)     |
| 3 | `94ead67` | the single install commit: 27 vendored files, two launchers, manifest   |
| 4 | `593218f` | `mix deps.update --all` -- six bumps, gates green either side           |
| 5 | `d6b14d0` | config: five built-ins off, `docs publish` wired to the real doc build  |
| 6 | `820da68` | the authored `docs` help topic                                          |

## What the project turned out to be

A paper and the small implementation it describes: one module, one test file, two dev-only deps (ex_doc, credo), no `bin/` at all, no application, no database, no CI. The substance is `docs/` -- a 24-document concept set, a blog set, an explainer set -- built by `docs/bin/publish`, a shell publisher over mdagg + pandoc + typst with a typst template and two lua pandoc filters. **The PDF is this project's build artefact**, which is why `docs publish` is the point of the install rather than a nicety on the end of it.

## The seals

Baseline sealed BEFORE `mix deps.update --all`, which is the whole point of the protocol's ordering.

    baseline  check  20260810-1006.{COMPILE,FORMAT,DEPS,TOOLCHAIN,CRITIC}.errors
              test   20260810-1007.{MIX,CREDO}.errors
    after     check  20260810-1007.{COMPILE,FORMAT,DEPS,TOOLCHAIN,CRITIC}.errors
              test   20260810-1007-46.MIX.errors, 20260810-1007-47.CREDO.errors
    docs      green  20260810-1011.PUBLISH.errors  (0 bytes)
              red    20260810-1010.PUBLISH.errors  (136 bytes -- called with no docset)

Every `.errors` seal above is 0 bytes except the last, which is deliberately red. `20260810-1007-46.MIX.out` and the baseline `20260810-1007.MIX.out` carry identical results, so the update moved nothing behind the suite.

**The baseline was already green**, so this project carried no drift at all: credo 1.7.16 -> 1.7.19, earmark_parser 1.4.44 -> 1.4.46, ex_doc 0.40.1 -> 0.40.3, jason 1.4.4 -> 1.4.5, makeup 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2, makeup_erlang 1.0.3 -> 1.1.0. Nothing to resolve. **This proves the protocol's SHAPE, not its strength** -- two dev-only deps is the gentlest test there is, and the record should not be read as the protocol having survived anything. Multiplyer's 1.18.0 / 27.0 pins are where it gets tested.

## The fence, proven rather than assumed

This project's pre-commit hook is not the fleet shape. It chains to Intent's critic gate and then runs raw `prettier --write` over every staged Markdown file, under `set -euo pipefail`. That is the issue-0008 blast radius exactly, so the fence was proven before the install depended on it, in three parts:

- **RED**: a deliberately misaligned probe `.md` under `bin/.devbin/lib/`, staged, hook run -- came back rewritten (sha changed).
- **GREEN**: same probe, same hook, fence in place -- byte-identical, hook exit 0.
- **SELECTIVE**: a project `.md` staged alongside the vendored one -- the vendored file untouched, the project file formatted normally. The fence is not a blanket disable.

The exit-code risk was real and is disproven: when every staged `.md` is ignored, prettier skips silently at rc 0, so the hook's `pipefail` does not abort a commit that stages only vendored Markdown.

Then the real proof, in the install commit itself: `bin/.devbin/lib/tmpl/help.md` is byte-identical afterwards (`123bf230...` before and after) and doctor reports the manifest intact. Issue 0008 does not recur here.

The authored help topic is the mirror case. `help/` is the PROJECT's half of the seam and is deliberately NOT fenced, so the hook formats it -- it was authored prettier-stable and proven byte-identical under `prettier --write` before the commit, and the hook confirmed it in the commit itself (`bin/.devbin/help/docs.md 15ms (unchanged)`).

## What the config had to say no to

The install offered sixteen commands; eleven survive. `server` (no Phoenix), `cli` (no escript, no `mix microgptex.cli`), `repl` (the builtin runs `mix <name>.cli repl`), `db` (no Ecto) and `build` (doctor's "offered with nothing to run") are each `enabled: false` with the reason recorded at the key. The test is whether a command is RUNNABLE, not whether it resolves -- an offered command that would fail is a surface that lies.

`build` was switched off rather than pointed at `mix compile`: compilation is already gated by `check compile` under `--warnings-as-errors`, and a second name for the same work is the Highlander breach.

## `docs publish` -- the composition question, answered

`docs` is a builtin gate whose only options had ever been `agents` and `treeindex`. A project option composes with them cleanly: `publish` appears first (declared before catalogue, same as Laksa's `check toolchain` ordering), `docs all` still synthesises, and `in_all: false` keeps publishing out of the argument-free sweep and REPORTS the exclusion. No base defect here -- the builtin's own header had already anticipated it ("`publish` ... encode[s] where a project keeps its generated output ... Those are project handlers").

The docset is passed through as trailing argv rather than enumerated in config, so the set of docsets stays declared once, in the publisher's own case statement. Called bare, the publisher's own usage line surfaces and the run seals red -- the sealed-gate contract holding over a script devbin did not write.

Demonstrated once end to end: `bin/mg docs publish 20-concepts` produced a 132KB aggregate and a 20MB PDF at v0.1.0, version taken from mix.exs per `version_from`.

## Dirt and facts surfaced, not fixed

- **The publisher does NOT sweep-format `docs/`.** Lamplight's publisher does (its `.prettierignore` names the damage), and this one is documented as "adapted from the Lamplight publisher", so it was checked rather than assumed. The tree is clean after a publish run.
- **`Icon\r` is not dirt.** The pre-flight survey reported it untracked-and-unignored; that test named the file `Icon` when the real name ends in a carriage return, so both `git ls-files` and `git check-ignore` missed. It is ignored, by `~/.gitignore_global:27`, in every project. The survey finding was wrong, and hv's call to check it in was made on it -- nothing was committed.
- **Intent version drift**: the project is on 2.13.0 against Devbin's 2.18.0. Out of this thread's scope; surfaced only.
- `check critic` iterates INTENT's declared languages (shell + elixir), not devbin's. That is correct -- Intent owns the critic language list -- and it is the clearest demonstration that the two `languages` lists are different facts.

# WP-05 inventory: Molt

## The finding that stops this WP as briefed

**`bin/molt` is Molt's product. It is not a dev launcher, and migrating it would delete the tool this project ships.**

WP-05's objective reads "Migrate Molt off its 179-line `bin/molt` launcher (plus `bin/bootstrap.sh`, 153 lines)", and its deliverables end "old launcher deleted last in its own commit". Following that would destroy the product.

The evidence is in the first fifteen lines of the file. `bin/molt` resolves its own symlink chain to find `MOLT_ROOT` (`bin/molt:7-12`) because it is invoked through a `~/bin/molt` symlink on every machine the user owns -- `README.md:53`, `README.md:142` (`MOLT_LOCAL_BIN` defaults to `~/bin`), and the `local-bin` liberator whose stated job is "`~/bin` directory, molt CLI symlink" (`README.md:165`). Its commands are the tool: `resleeve`, `upgrade`, `maintain`, `new-user`, `status`, `list`, `git`.

`bin/bootstrap.sh` is worse to touch. It is the **public installer**, documented as a curl one-liner against a raw GitHub URL:

    MOLT_PRJ_DIR=$HOME/Projects bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/you/molt/main/bin/bootstrap.sh)

That is `README.md:82`. The path is an external contract with anyone who has ever copied that line. It is not a dev script and it is not this thread's to move.

**How the brief went wrong**: the 2026-08-10 survey counted lines in `bin/` and classified by size. 179 + 153 lines in `bin/` reads as a launcher fleet. Nothing in the survey opened the files. This is the third stale brief in the thread -- WP-02 and WP-03 were both reclassified at WP start -- but the first where the deliverables were actively destructive rather than merely mis-sized.

## What this project actually is: the same shape hv parked

Molt is a **beside-the-product** project, which is WP-06's shape:

> **PARKED by hv, 2026-08-10: the beside-the-product shape needs more thought before devbin enters Utilz.**

And WP-06's dependency line reads "WP-05 (shell shape proven); hv's naming ruling" -- the sequencing assumed WP-05 would prove the straightforward shell migration first, and that WP-06 was the one hard case. **There is no straightforward shell migration in this thread.** Molt and Utilz are the same problem, and the easy predecessor that was supposed to de-risk it does not exist.

This is a ruling for hv, not a builder's reclassification. Reshaping AC-05.4 from "switch, delete last" to "delete nothing" is scope change, and the beside-the-product shape is explicitly parked.

## Command dispositions -- all eleven

Exactly one command in `bin/molt` is dev tooling. Every other one is the product.

| command      | kind    | disposition                                                              |
| ------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `resleeve`   | product | stays -- bootstraps a machine from the user's stack                      |
| `upgrade`    | product | stays -- pulls repos, runs upgrade hooks                                 |
| `maintain`   | product | stays -- brew update, doom upgrade, per-liberator maintenance            |
| `new-user`   | product | stays -- scaffolds a `molt-{user}` config repo                           |
| `status`     | product | stays -- sleeve state and liberator status                               |
| `list`       | product | stays -- liberator enabled/disabled/installed                            |
| `git`        | product | stays -- runs a git command across all managed repos                     |
| `doctor`     | product | stays -- checks `MOLT_HOME` and machine state; NAME collides, see below  |
| `version`    | product | stays -- name collides with the devbin builtin                           |
| `help`       | product | stays -- name collides with the devbin builtin                           |
| `test`       | **dev** | **the only overlap** -- shellcheck + bats over this repo's own `test/`   |

`cmd_test` (`lib/molt.sh:601-621`) requires `bats`, runs `_test_shellcheck` first, then the suite under `test/`, optionally scoped to one liberator. That is precisely what devbin's shell test and check arms do. It is the one real Highlander question in this project, and it is one command, not a 179-line fleet.

`bin/bootstrap.sh`: **stays, untouched, and is out of scope**. Its own disposition was a named deliverable of this WP ("migrate, keep beside, or delete -- ruled in the inventory, not assumed"). Ruled: keep beside. It is a published install path, not dev tooling.

### The three name collisions are not a devbin problem

`doctor`, `version` and `help` exist on both sides, but they answer about different subjects: `molt doctor` checks the user's machine, `devbin doctor` checks the devbin install. They only collide for a human reading two help texts, and only if devbin is given a name a user would type by accident. The alias ruling below is what keeps them apart.

## The collision probe -- run, and the base is correct

WP-06's first deliverable asks what `devbin install` does when `bin/<name>` already exists and is not a devbin symlink: *"refuse-or-skip is right, a clobber is a base defect to file before proceeding."* Molt has exactly that collision, so the probe was run here, in a throwaway `git clone`, never against the live repo.

**The base refuses, and says so.** `lib/cmd/install:69-95` (`link_alias`) is explicit, and its comment names this exact scenario -- *"On a migration the thing sitting there is the hand-written launcher devbin is replacing, and clobbering it would destroy the only copy of the thing being ported from"*. Observed rather than inferred:

    devbin: bin/molt already exists and is not a symlink -- leaving it alone
    devbin:   (rename it, then re-run, if you want devbin to answer to that name)
      linked     bin/mt -> devbin

After the install, in the clone:

- `git diff --stat` empty and `git status` showing only untracked additions -- **every tracked product file byte-untouched**
- `bin/molt version` still prints `MOLT v0.1.1`
- `bin/bootstrap.sh` untouched
- `bin/devbin doctor`: **8 checks, 0 failed, 3 notes**

The doctor note is the part worth keeping:

    note  launcher: bin/molt exists and is not a devbin symlink

It surfaces the coexistence instead of hiding it. **No base defect to file.** The beside-the-product shape is mechanically safe today; what is unresolved about it is a naming and ownership question, not a code question.

## What is left for hv to rule

1. **Does WP-05 become a beside-the-product install, or does it park beside WP-06?** They are the same shape. Parking one and running the other needs a reason.
2. **The alias.** `bin/molt` is taken and stays taken. The probe used `mt`; `bin/devbin` alone is also viable and collides with nothing. Same question WP-06 has open ("no `bin/utilz` symlink; alias `uz` suggested, or none").
3. **`molt test` -- does it stay, or does the repo's own test surface move to devbin?** This is the only genuine Highlander overlap. It is a product command that ships to users AND the way this repo tests itself; those two roles can be split, but splitting them changes the product's surface.

Nothing has been installed into the live Molt repo. The only change made there is unrelated and already committed (`46231e7`, removing a stale `elixir` language declaration).

Written before `scripts/` was deleted, and every row RUN rather than reasoned.

The rule this pack is built to obey (WP-02's lesson, the hard way): **for every row, name the claim that could FAIL, and test THAT.** A true statement in an evidence column is worse than an empty one, because an empty one still looks unfinished. Where a row's evidence is a true statement about something adjacent, it is marked as such.

Seals quoted below are named; counts come from those seals and nowhere else.

## The twelve entries

## The rows, with their evidence

### `cli` -- the prefix was redundant, and dropping it RESTORES a broken override

The claim that could fail was "the `REPL_MODE=true` prefix is load-bearing for `mix prolix.cli`". Four runs of the same command, `about`, stdout only:

    env -u REPL_MODE mix prolix.cli about      84 bytes
    env REPL_MODE=true mix prolix.cli about    84 bytes   byte-identical
    env REPL_MODE=false mix prolix.cli about  971 bytes   console logs appear
    ./scripts/cli about                        84 bytes
    REPL_MODE=false ./scripts/cli about        84 bytes   IDENTICAL to plain

Redundant, because `Mix.Tasks.Prolix.Cli` sets `REPL_MODE` in its own MODULE BODY when unset (`lib/mix/tasks/prolix_cli.ex:7-9`), before `app.config` loads.

The fourth and fifth rows are the finding. `REPL_MODE=false` is this project's own documented override -- "Explicit override: show all logs to console, no file backend", implemented at `lib/prolix/application.ex:27-29` and again in `runtime.exs`, and named as a supported feature in its own completed ST0011. **The old script made it unreachable**, because a command-prefix assignment wins over the caller's environment. The builtin passes the environment through, so it works again.

So the migration did not merely preserve `cli`. It repaired it. That was not the expected result and it is the reason AC-08.6 said probe rather than reason.

### `iex` -- load-bearing, and proven so in the opposite direction

Same probe piped into `iex -S mix`, counting console log lines:

    env -u REPL_MODE iex -S mix     RM=nil      11 console log lines
    env REPL_MODE=true iex -S mix   RM="true"    0 console log lines

Nothing on this path runs a mix task, so nothing sets the variable. Carried as `run: env REPL_MODE=true iex -S mix`.

`env`, not a bare assignment: a config `run:` is word-split and deliberately never eval'd (`lib/resolve`), so a leading `REPL_MODE=true` would be taken as the NAME of a command to execute. That is the D1 boundary, and it is why this needed `env` rather than a transcription of the old line.

### `repl` -- rlwrap wiring, proven by poisoning rlwrap

The claim that could fail was "the completions data no longer reaches rlwrap". A fake `rlwrap` first on PATH, echoing its arguments:

    RLWRAP-ARGS: -f /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Prolix/bin/completions/repl.txt \
                 -r -c -H /Users/matts/.prolix_repl_history -s 2000 \
                 mix prolix.cli repl

The old script passed `-f <completions> --complete-filenames` and no history at all. The builtin passes the completions file, `-r -c`, a persistent history file and a 2000-line scrollback. **Strictly more than the old script, not less** -- which is the comparison worth making, since a port that quietly does less passes every test you would think to write.

### `completions/` -- byte-identical across the move

Moved at `81de3fa`. The first comparison attempted here was VACUOUS and is recorded as such: `git show HEAD~4:scripts/completions/completions.txt` returned nothing, because the file had already moved by that revision, and the md5 of nothing (`d41d8cd9...`) reads exactly like a real answer. Redone against the actual move commit:

    81de3fa~1:scripts/completions/completions.txt   adfc7fc40e7e3b6eb5e63b4bb094afa1
    81de3fa:bin/completions/repl.txt                adfc7fc40e7e3b6eb5e63b4bb094afa1
    working tree                                    adfc7fc40e7e3b6eb5e63b4bb094afa1

That near-miss is the pack's own instance of the rule at the top of this file: an md5 of an empty stream is a true statement about nothing.

### `server` -- proven live, not by inspection

`bin/prolix server` was started and `http://localhost:4000/api` answered within one second. It was then used as the fixture for the swift arm, which is a stronger check than a start-and-stop: the iOS suite's failures moved from `Could not connect to the server` to `loginFailed`, so the server was not merely up, it was serving this project's API.

### `test` -- `--trace` is a recorded delta, and still reachable

The gate runs plain `mix test`; the old script ran `mix test --trace` always. `--trace` forces synchronous execution and prints every test name, which is a debugging mode rather than a gate default, so it is not carried.

The claim that could fail is "`--trace` is no longer reachable". Undeclared options pass through to the tool:

    $ bin/prolix test mix --trace test/cli/cli_fixtures_test.exs
      * test match_management/051 [L#9]  * test match_management/051 (435.2ms) [L#9]
      ...
      Finished in 7.6 seconds (0.00s async, 7.6s sync)
      Result: 23 passed
      verdict: tmp/test/20260810-2035.MIX.errors

Trace format present, `0.00s async` confirming synchronous execution, and it sealed.

### `mix` -- not ported, because with the dead prefix gone it wraps nothing

`LAKSA_CONFIG_PATH` / `LAKSA_CONFIG_FILE` prefixed three scripts. Remove them and `scripts/mix` is `mix $*`.

**The inventory's conclusion was right and its stated reason was FALSE, and the reason is what generalises.** The inventory said "nothing under `lib/`, `config/` or `test/` mentions `LAKSA_CONFIG`". `config/.env` does, on lines 2 and 3, and it is a TRACKED file loaded by `config/runtime.exs:13` in dev and test.

The correct reason is one level down. `arca_config` resolves `<DOMAIN>_CONFIG_PATH` where the domain is `Application.get_env(:arca_config, :config_domain)`, and Prolix sets `config_domain: :prolix` (`config/config.exs:187`, again at `lib/prolix/application.ex:18`). So the live variables are `PROLIX_CONFIG_PATH` / `PROLIX_CONFIG_FILE` -- which is exactly what `lib/prolix/config.ex:38-40` documents. Checked by name, all three read by nothing:

    LAKSA_MAILERSEND_TOKEN     read by NOTHING
    LAKSA_MAILERSEND_INUSE     read by NOTHING
    LAKSA_CONFIG_PATH          read by NOTHING

This is arca_config's `ARCA_CONFIG_PATH=.arca` a second time and one layer worse: there the dead setting was only in the scripts, so deleting them removed it. **Here it is also in the committed `.env`, so deleting `scripts/` does NOT remove the dead setting from this project.** It stays, in a tracked file, named for a different project. Surfaced, not fixed -- see the findings section.

### `echo` -- broken, and proven broken before being binned

    $ find . -name "echo_task.exs" -not -path "./deps/*" -not -path "./_build/*"
    (no output)

`scripts/echo` ends `./scripts/mix run scripts/echo_task.exs`. The file it runs does not exist anywhere in the repository. It cannot have worked since that file went away, and nobody noticed -- the same story as arca_cli's `update_completions` and Multiplyer's dead SIA pipeline. An unexercised path stays green by never being run.

### `taillog` -- ported with two deltas, both deliberate

Rewritten rather than moved verbatim; both deltas are in the handler's own header.

1. Defaults to `PROJECT_ROOT` rather than the caller's cwd. The dispatcher execs a handler without cd'ing, so the old `${1:-.}` resolved against wherever you were standing: from `lib/` it looked for `lib/.lib/logs`. The old script was correct only when run from the root. An explicit argument still wins.
2. The three error messages name the path actually looked at. They said `in .currentdir/logs` literally, with the real directory computed one line above and then not used.

### `dbproxy` -- one config line

`run: fly proxy 5433:5433 --app prolix-db`, registered and shown in help under Surfaces. The old script echoed its own command line before running it; not carried, because this is a foreground proxy you watch rather than a gate that seals.

### `flysql` -- MOVED, and git says so

The claim that could fail was "the credential ended up in a second file". It did not:

    $ git show --stat <port commit>
    rename {scripts => bin/.devbin/cmd}/flysql (63%)

**`R`, a rename, not add-plus-delete.** `git log --follow` is continuous across the move and the `DB_PASS` line was never retyped. The 63% similarity is the header added above it, not the body.

`taillog` shows as add+delete by contrast, because it was rewritten. That difference is the point rather than an inconsistency: the move-not-copy rule was always about the credential specifically, so that the rotation hv has deferred stays a one-file edit.

## Callers followed before deletion

| caller                       | was                                              | now                       |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml`   | a `Make scripts executable` step chmod'ing three | step DELETED -- see below |
| `priv/repo/seeds_prod.exs:4` | `Requires dbproxy running: scripts/dbproxy`      | `bin/prolix dbproxy`      |
| `intent/st/COMPLETED/ST0011` | describes `scripts/cli` and `scripts/repl`       | LEFT ALONE, deliberately  |

The CI step chmod'd `scripts/test`, `scripts/cli` and `scripts/repl` and **CI never invoked any of them** -- it runs `mix test`, `mix compile`, `mix format` and `mix credo` directly. So the step made three files executable for nobody, and would have failed the build the moment they were deleted. Removed rather than repointed.

ST0011 is a COMPLETED steel thread describing what was true when it ran. It is a historical record, not documentation of current behaviour, and rewriting history to match today is how a record stops being one.

## Findings surfaced, not fixed

These came out of the equivalence work and are recorded for hv rather than actioned. None is a devbin finding.

1. **`config/.env` is TRACKED and holds a live third-party credential.** A MailerSend API token, committed, in a file `.gitignore` does not cover. It sits under `LAKSA_MAILERSEND_TOKEN`, which **nothing reads** -- the code reads unprefixed `MAILERSEND_TOKEN` (`lib/prolix/email/adapters/mailersend_rest.ex:12`, `config/runtime.exs:200`). Exposed and inert at once, which is precisely why it went unnoticed. `b47f3f0 Restore config/.env for CI/CD tests` shows it was once removed and deliberately put back.

2. **`priv/repo/seeds_prod.exs:2` carries the `prolix` database password** in a `DATABASE_URL` in a comment.

   With `scripts/flysql`, that is **three committed credentials across three files**, in three different shapes. hv's 2026-08-10 ruling covered the geodica-db one specifically ("proceed as if rotated"; all repositories private; rotate the sharing projects together, later). It does not automatically extend to a MailerSend token or the prolix DB password, which are different services with different blast radii. Raised as a pattern rather than three items, because the pattern is the finding.

   The APNs signing key was CHECKED and is fine: `config/.creds/` is gitignored at `.gitignore:41` and `git ls-files` returns nothing for it.

3. **CI's credo step examines nothing.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:113` runs `mix credo --only error`:

       Analysis took 0.03 seconds (0.03s to load, 0.00s running 0 checks on 267 files)
       1717 mods/funs, found no issues.

   credo has no `error` category, so `--only error` matches zero checks, and the step has reported "found no issues" over 267 unexamined files for as long as it has existed. It reads like someone chose a severity. **Third project in the fleet with this exact invocation.** Not changed here: the real gate (`bin/prolix test credo`) is red at 228 findings, and sizing that is hv's call, as it was at arca_cli.

4. **The deploy image trails the pins.** `check toolchain` is red on the image arm: `.tool-versions` pins 1.20.3 / 29.0.5, the Dockerfile builds 1.19.3 / 28.2. Deploy-affecting, so hv's, and hv already owes this project a deploy carrying the Oban v14 migration.

5. **`check format` is red at 632 sealed findings** across 78 Swift files, on an app that is on the App Store. `fmt swift` would clear it and rewrite 50 files / 677 insertions; measured and reverted rather than kept.

Written before any code, per the extend-ACs-before-code rule, and after the Molt lesson: every entry below was **read**, not sized.

## STOP FIRST: a live production credential is committed to this repository

**`scripts/flysql:15` contains a plaintext password for the `geodica-db` cluster**, together with the cluster address and user. It is not Prolix-scoped: the script's own `DB_MAP` opens `conflab_prod`, `laksa_prod` and `prolix_prod`, so the credential reaches **three production databases across three projects**.

It is in git history, so deleting the file does not remove it -- `git log -S` finds it in two commits, `f21484b` ("Add flysql script for geodica-db MPG access") and `5f78f3b`. **Rotation is the only fix that fixes anything, and it is hv's call entirely.**

**hv's ruling, 2026-08-10: proceed as if rotated.** Every affected repository is private; several unrelated private projects share this managed PG instance, and hv will rotate them all on one day, after this work lands, so that the change is single and coordinated rather than piecemeal. hv's own words: *"it is (very) bad practice, I know, and so I will fix it. Just not now."* Recorded as a deliberate, informed deferral rather than an oversight.

This is not a devbin finding and this WP does not resolve it. It is recorded here because the migration would otherwise have **copied the credential into a new file** -- a `bin/.devbin/cmd/` handler or a `config.yaml` `run:` line -- which turns one exposure into two and puts a fresh timestamp on it. **One rule survives the ruling, and it is the reason this section stays at the top: the credential is MOVED, never COPIED.** Porting `flysql` means `git mv` into its handler, not transcribing it. A copy would put the same secret in a second file with a fresh timestamp and make rotation day a hunt instead of a one-file edit. Deleting the script is still not this WP's call either -- deletion without rotation removes nothing, since git history holds it regardless.

## What this WP is, versus what its brief said

**Prolix is a `scripts/` MIGRATION, not the fresh install the brief describes.** It has no `bin/` directory at all and a twelve-entry, 235-line `scripts/` fleet. This is the same staleness that hit WP-02 and WP-03 (mis-sized, harmless) and WP-05 (destructive). Corrected before starting, not at close.

The brief's `Dependencies` line also reads "The elixir protocol (WP-01) and, softly, everything before it". **WP-01 is cancelled.** The elixir protocol was in fact proven at WP-02, WP-03 and WP-04, all of which are done, so the dependency is satisfied by different work than it names.

Confirmed as briefed, and still true: `native/ios/Prolix.xcodeproj` exists, `Dockerfile` and `fly.toml` exist, and there is no root `.tool-versions`.

**What is NOT true any more: Prolix is no longer "last on top of a by-then boring elixir path".** It is the only WP left in the thread. Molt was to have proven the shell shape ahead of it and is cancelled, so `shell` and `swift` gate scope both reach this WP unexercised, on the project that also carries the first live deploy-image arm.

## `REPL_MODE` is LIVE here, and the arca_cli precedent does not transfer

At arca_cli, `REPL_MODE` was dropped, and not as a judgement call -- that project's own `dead_code_gate_test.exs` asserts zero sites for it. **Prolix is the opposite.** `lib/prolix/application.ex:27-36` and `:101-108` branch on it to choose console versus file logging, and `lib/prolix/cli.ex:74` sets it. It is load-bearing.

So the `REPL_MODE=true` prefix in `scripts/cli` and `scripts/iex` **is carried**, not dropped. Reusing arca_cli's disposition here would have silently removed working behaviour -- the same shape of error as reusing a stale caller survey, and the reason a per-project inventory is not a formality.

One thing to establish at equivalence rather than assert now: `lib/prolix/cli.ex:74` sets `REPL_MODE` itself, so the prefix may be redundant for `cli` while remaining load-bearing for `iex -S mix`, which runs no task. **Probe it; do not reason about it.**
